definitions.explanation: A casual establishment where people go to drink alcohol, typically serving food as well. Covers a range of places from small standing bars to izakaya-style pubs.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{飲|の}み{屋|や}に{行|い}こう。
examples.english: Let's go to the bar near the station.

examples.japanese: この{通|とお}りには{飲|の}み{屋|や}がたくさん{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: There are many bars lined up along this street.

examples.japanese: {昨日|きのう}は{会社|かいしゃ}の{同僚|どうりょう}と{飲|の}み{屋|や}で{遅|おそ}くまで{話|はな}していた。
examples.english: Yesterday I was talking late at a bar with my coworkers.

notes:
USAGE:
A casual, everyday word for places where people drink alcohol. More colloquial than {居酒屋|いざかや}, which specifically refers to Japanese-style pubs. {飲|の}み{屋|や} can refer to any type of drinking establishment, from a tiny {立|た}ち{飲|の}み (standing bar) to a larger pub.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {飲|の}み{屋|や}に{行|い}く (to go to a bar)
- {行|い}きつけの{飲|の}み{屋|や} (one's regular bar)
- {飲|の}み{屋|や}{街|がい} (bar district)
- {安|やす}い{飲|の}み{屋|や} (cheap bar)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {居酒屋|いざかや}: Japanese-style pub — more specific, often used as a business name
- バー: bar — suggests a Western-style establishment
- {酒場|さかば}: drinking place — slightly literary or old-fashioned
